title: Phase 2: Input validation hardening for _resolve_date()
outcome: Successfully implemented Phase 2 of the analytics skill bug fixes plan. Hardened _resolve_date() to reject literal 'None' string, invalid date formats, and impossible dates. Added _parse_or_default() helper function with date validation via date.fromisoformat(). All 92 tests pass (76 existing + 16 new).
key_decisions: Extracted _parse_or_default() as a pure helper function (only side effect: logging warning on invalid input) following SRP
Used date.fromisoformat() for date validation instead of regex, leveraging stdlib for correctness
Rejected literal 'None' string (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed) to prevent str(None) bugs from propagating to SQL queries
Added logging import and module-level logger to utils.py, consistent with other query modules (git_commits.py, daily_git.py)
Invalid dates fall back to default with a logged warning rather than raising ValueError, maintaining backward compatibility
learnings: The existing truthiness documentation test (checking for 'truthiness'/'falsy'/'empty string'/'fall through' keywords in comments) still passes because the new comments describe the same behavior with different wording — good test resilience
When mocking logger.warning, call_args[0] is the format string, not the interpolated message — need to check the full args tuple
The _resolve_date function was previously documented as passing 'None' string through as a valid date — this was a known bug that Phase 2 finally fixes
next_steps: Phase 3: Model pricing completeness — add 4 missing models to MODEL_PRICING
Phase 4: Documentation and disclaimer — cache hit rate clarification in HTML report
